title: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the Permanent Labor Certification Immigrant Visa Program
pass_4_primary_concern: Inconsistent recruitment and filing deadlines can prevent otherwise compliant employers from submitting valid applications.
pass_5_high_stakes_domain_reason: The program affects access to permanent employment-based immigration, livelihoods and worker displacement; former Schedule A healthcare staffing can also affect service continuity. This does not establish any particular shortage or patient outcome.
pass_5_concise_why: The worker-protection purpose fits the general recruitment reforms. Material concerns are incompatible filing clocks, a broadly restrictive layoff screen with limited comparative evidence, and an unreliable low-cost recruitment baseline. These are specific, potentially repairable defects; the record does not establish bad faith or a wholesale failure of the program.
pass_5_most_important_consequence: Employers may lose a filing opportunity or repeat recruitment because the calendar is unclear, while laid-off U.S. workers may receive protections that are poorly targeted and sponsored workers face additional delay. Staffing effects depend on local conditions and are not quantified here.
